units.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,41 @@
+# number: 63
+# tmt:
+#   summary: Install from a shared mount namespace without leaking the storage bind mount
+#   duration: 30m
+# extra:
+#   # bootloader=none is not supported for composefs (see test-install-no-boot-dir.nu)
+#   fixme_skip_if_composefs: true
+#
+# Regression test for https://github.com/bootc-dev/bootc/issues/2455
+#
+# Installing with --source-imgref skips bootc's own mount namespace unshare,
+# so on a host where / is shared (the systemd default) the bind mount made
+# for podman onto /run/bootc/storage used to propagate back and stay mounted.
+# run_install already uses MountFlags=slave, which hides that, so make /
+# shared again inside that namespace before installing.
+
+use std assert
+use tap.nu
+
+def main [] {
+    tap begin "install to-filesystem with shared mount propagation"
+
+    bootc image copy-to-storage
+    let target_image = "containers-storage:localhost/bootc"
+
+    mkdir /var/mnt
+    truncate -s 10G disk.img
+    mkfs.ext4 disk.img
+    mount -o loop disk.img /var/mnt
+
+    setenforce 0
+
+    tap run_install $"mount --make-rshared /
+bootc install to-filesystem --disable-selinux --bootloader=none --source-imgref ($target_image) /var/mnt
+if findmnt /run/bootc/storage; then echo 'error: /run/bootc/storage mount leaked'; exit 1; fi"

units.body: I think this is fine, but probably going forward we should actually prefer `SLAVE` so we do pick up mounts from the host into our mountns. But it's unlikely to matter because the process here is short-lived.
Hmm...I think we should be doing the unshare in the `to-existing-root` case most likely too.

Someone else already tried to do a similar PR right? I don't like this because it just basically disables part of the gpt auto generator behind its back.

The fix that seems cleanest to me is something like changing the systemd generator to prefer mounting at `/efi` first (and we create that dir).

Alternatively though here, we could try reverting the change to have the `/boot` bind mount and change our logic so that we always handle the case of being in a running sysroot and look at that path. That feels...tractable. It's effectively reverting the PR that added this bind mount in the first place of course and we'd need to go back through the rationale and ensure this doesn't break anything.

     return glnx_throw_errno_prefix (error, "symlinkat");
 
+  /* When it can find the root disk, systemd-gpt-auto-generator sees our

+   * automount then fronts our bind mount: once idle it unmounts /boot (and
+   * stops local-fs.target, which requires boot.mount), and at shutdown
+   * stopping it detaches /boot underneath ostree-finalize-staged.service.
+   * /boot is ours here, so mask the automount.
